# v3.02.115 SSLP115 - Calculation of the energy return rate of a cracked disc in the presence of initial stresses

**Summary**

This test validates the calculation of the energy return rate by the theta method in the presence of a state of initial stress.

**Model A:** a clamped disc and cracked is subjected to an initial stress field opening the crack. This initial stress field is identical to that generated by a thermal gradient. The solution is identical to that obtained in the case of thermal loading alone, validating the consideration of an initial stress state.

**Modelling B:** it is similar to Modelling A with a non-grided crack (X-FEM).

**Modelling** **C:** it is similar to Modelling A. Material coefficients are defined by constant temperature functions.

## 1 Reference problem

### 1.1 Geometry

A $\mathrm{100mm}$ ray disc, clamped on its edges, containing a horizontal crack of $\mathrm{23mm}$, one of which is at the centre of the disc, is considered.

![Figure](/figures/v3.02.115/10000000000002340000019968BA48067ED88EB3.png)

Figure 1.1: Géométrie du disque.

.

### 1.2 Material properties

Young's modulus:    $E=210000\mathrm{MPa}$

Poisson's ratio:    $\nu =0,3$

Thermal expansion coefficient: $\alpha ={10}^{-5}{K}^{-1}$

### 1.3 Boundary conditions and loads

The disc is totally clamped on its edge.

It is subjected to an initial stress field obtained by applying a thermal load with a strong gradient in the horizontal direction (see and ).

![Figure](/figures/v3.02.115/10000000000002210000013E228E42EC6C041CD3.png)

Figure 1.2: Gradient de température appliqué au disque encastré.

![Figure](/figures/v3.02.115/1000000000000275000000F57537E6AC30CDA8CB.png)

Figure 1.3: Création du champ de contraintes initiales.

### 1.4 reference solution

The reference solution is the one obtained by applying the thermal load directly to the cracked disc without initial condition. Indeed, since the behaviour is elastic, the superposition principle applies and the results in the presence of thermal loading without initial stresses and in the absence of thermal stresses with initial stresses are equivalent, as summarized in .

![Figure](/figures/v3.02.115/10000000000002150000022E7555234486A4683F.png)

Figure 1.4: Équivalence des chargements.

## 2 Modelling A

### 2.1 Mesh characteristics

The mesh is quadratic radiating around the crack; it consists of 27670 nodes forming 9519 mesh cells, 100 triangles allowing de-refining. The mesh cells are quadratic. elements type "Barsium" are used at both bottoms of the crack. The mesh used and have the mesh.

![Figure](/figures/v3.02.115/100000000000022B000001542E935338CDEBC37F.png)

Figure 2.1: Maillage du disque.

![Figure](/figures/v3.02.115/100000000000025F00000125B9F71662DF604DAE.png)

Figure 2.2: Maillage : zoom sur la fissure.

From the mesh, several crowns are defined which will be used later, during the post-processing in the break-up mechanics. Each crown is characterized by the data of a lower radius (R_INF) and a higher radius (R_SUP). The correspondence is also given in terms of the number of layers d

|  | Value of R_INF (mm) | Value of R_SUP (mm) | Number of layers correspondence d |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Crown No. 1 | 1,009 | 2,05 | 2h-4h |
| Crown No. 2 | 2,05 | 4,228 | 4h-8h |
| Crown No. 3 | 4,228 | 9,0 | 8h-16h |

### 2.2 Calculations

It is recalled that the principle of this test to verify equivalence between the consideration of an initial state and an equivalent thermal load, when post-processing of the mechanical failure is used.

The quantities of interest is the energy return rate (G) and stress intensity factors (limited here to KI because configuration only requires mode I due to symmetry). Paragraph 2.3.1 details the different ways to post-treat those quantities that are used and tested.

*Modelization* : The configuration is bidimental. Mechanical calculations are performed under the hypothesis of Planes Deformations.

*Reference scale:*

Since analytical solution is not known, the first step is to generate the calculation as the reference: i.e. the thermo-linear elasticity calculation. The creation of the temperature field is followed by the thermo-elastic bonding calculation, following which two types of post-processings are made:

- a post-processing in breaking mechanics to determine the reference values of the quantities of interest,
- extraction of the stress field, which will serve as the initial stress field.

*Calculum with initial constraints:*

An incremental linear elasticity calculation with an initial state given as an initial stress field, with the presence of the crack, is performed. It is important to note that **l-initial state is specified** **via an initial stress field** , not by the result type (EVOL_NOLI) concept data in the resolution operator.

Then, post-processings in breaker mechanics are made. To test the different possibilities offered by the CALC_G command, several configurations are implemented, which differ by the type of initial stress field provided to the CALC_G command: at Gauss points, nodes by element or nodes.

### 2.3 Tested quantities and results

#### 2.3.1 Quantities tested

The values of the energy return rate (G) from:

- CALC_G operator, option G.

The values of the stress intensity factor in mode I (KI) obtained from:

- CALC_G operator, option K,
- POST_K1_K2_K3 operator.

For post-processings with CALC_G operator, the 3 previously defined crowns are systematically tested.

Finally, each time, the values from the reference calculation were compared to the values from the initial state calculation, with iso-condition (the same representation of the initial stress field, the same operator of post-processing, the same crown).

## 3 Modelling B

### 3.1 Mesh characteristics

The geometry is identical to model A. The mesh represents the blank part of any crack (it will be represented by the X-FEM method); the mesh is linear.

### 3.2 Calculations

To test the different possibilities offered by the CALC_G_XFEM command, several calculation configurations are implemented.

The first is the reference result obtained by thermal loading without initial condition.

The rest are derived from the initial state calculation without thermal loading; they differ from the values of the crown rays supplied to the CALC_G_XFEM control. As for Modelling A, stress intensity factors are also tested (reference is obtained by POST_K1_K2_K3). It is noted that only the initial stress field at the gauss points was used, since the definition of a stress field at nodes is not available with X-FEM.

### 3.3 Tested quantities and results

#### 3.3.1 Quantities tested

The value of the operator's energy return rate shall be tested, all of which shall be equal to a low tolerance.

## 4 Modelling C

This Modelling, added for computer validation purposes, tests the possibility of using temperature-dependent material coefficients.

It is identical to model A. The only difference is that the material coefficients are defined by constant temperature functions.

## 5 Summary of the results

The test case allows a comparison of the results obtained from a thermal loading and an initial stress field. It shows that the results are substantially equivalent.

More precisely in FEM (modelization A):

- Conclusions on G:

  - Excellent independence of CALC_G results to crowns (maximum difference between crowns less than 0.004%), in any case,
  - Strictly identical results between an initial stress field provided to CALC_G of type ELGA and ELNO,
  - Results very close to the reference, with the same crown (difference less than 0.01%). The closest results are obtained when the initial stress is given to nodes at CALC_G,
- Conclusions on K:

  - Same conclusions as on G, with each time a double accuracy (maximum difference between crowns less than 0.002% and difference at reference less than 0.005%)

It should be added that this same case gives the same results with the Abaqus software in version 6.11 (method FEM, G calculation only).
